text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish ships receive an increasing number of complaints about poor safety from maritime authorities in foreign ports.
- Carl Cederschioeld, a conservative member of the Stockholm police board, says the Hells Angels and other motorcycle clubs should have their telephones bugged.
- Social Welfare Minister Margot Wallstroem says she is unsure if it would be wise to enter EMU now because it might jeopardise Swedish welfare policies.
- The Social Democratic Party's executive committee will probably recommend to the party congress that Sweden join EMU sometime after 1999, a SIFO opinion poll shows.
- Scandinavian airline SAS accounts for about 11 percent of the passenger volumes and turnover of the new five-member Star Alliance, which was signed on Wednesday.
- Housing construction in the first quarter is at its lowest level for 60 years, according to the Central Bureau of Statistics.
- The number of workers in major Swedish industrial companies increased in 1995 after four years of cuts.
- Sweden's competition authority is launching an investigation into the proposed merger between Swedish construction groups NCC and Siab which could threaten the deal.
- Swedish-Italian Salvatore Grimaldi, managing director of Swedish bicycle company Monark Stiga, went to Italy to visit his latest acquisition, the Bianchi bike company.
- Furniture giant IKEA will help the government by creating 30,000 jobs in Sweden. One way the company plans to do this is by purchasing more Swedish-made goods.
